info.name: PSPF EDMS API
info.description:
Full route coverage for the PSPF Electronic Document & Records Management System backend.

Run order for a clean end-to-end pass:
1. Auth > Register (or use a seeded user from pspf_edms_seed_test_data.sql)
2. Auth > Login  (captures accessToken/refreshToken, or mfaToken if the role requires MFA)
3. MFA > (enroll + confirm, or verify challenge) if prompted
4. Folders > Create Folder (captures folderId)
5. Documents > Register Document (captures documentId)
6. Versions / Permissions / Approvals / Workflow / Audit / Retention / Reports / Integrations / Notifications / Users as needed

All requests use collection variables set automatically by the Test scripts on Login/MFA/Create endpoints — you normally don't need to edit anything by hand.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Creates an account directly. In production this is normally disabled/admin-only — kept for a working dev flow.

Use a seeded account (see database/pspf_edms_seed_test_data.sql) or one you registered. If the role requires MFA, response contains mfaRequired, mfaEnrollmentRequired, availableMethods, and mfaToken — check the Postman Console (View > Show Postman Console) after sending this for a printed instruction on exactly which MFA request to run next.

exec: ? ">>> Next: MFA > 'Enroll TOTP (login) - Start', then '...- Confirm'. Do NOT call Verify TOTP yet — nothing is enrolled."
: ">>> Next: MFA > 'Verify TOTP (login)' (or Send SMS/Email Challenge, then Verify SMS/Email OTP).");
console.log("MFA required — mfaToken saved. Use the MFA folder to complete sign-in.");

item.name: MFA

request.description: FIRST STEP for an account with no authenticator enrolled yet (login response had mfaEnrollmentRequired: true). Uses the interim mfaToken from Login — not a full accessToken, because the account can't get one until MFA is satisfied. Returns { qrDataUrl, base32Secret }. Scan qrDataUrl (base64 PNG) in any TOTP app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, etc.), or type base32Secret in manually.

SECOND STEP: enter the current 6-digit code your authenticator app is showing for the secret from 'Enroll TOTP (login) — Start'. On success this ALSO completes sign-in (returns accessToken/refreshToken), same as Verify TOTP does — no separate verify call needed.

exec: console.log("MFA required — mfaToken saved. Use the MFA folder to complete sign-in.");

request.description: For a user who is ALREADY fully signed in and wants to add/replace an authenticator (e.g. new phone). Different from the pair above: this needs a real accessToken, which only exists after MFA is already satisfied once.
Requires a full accessToken (already signed in) — backup codes are a recovery mechanism generated from within Security & Access, not something you can create before your first successful sign-in.

Only works if the backend's SMS_PROVIDER/Twilio credentials are configured and reachable. If you're offline or those aren't set up, use the TOTP enroll/verify requests instead — they need no external network call at all.
Only works if the backend's SMTP credentials are configured and reachable. Same offline caveat as Send SMS Challenge.

Only call this if mfaEnrollmentRequired was FALSE at login (an authenticator is already enrolled and verified). If you get 'TOTP is not enrolled for this account', that means mfaEnrollmentRequired was actually true — go run 'Enroll TOTP (login) — Start' and '— Confirm' instead, this account has never completed enrolment.

exec: console.log("MFA required — mfaToken saved. Use the MFA folder to complete sign-in.");
console.log("MFA required — mfaToken saved. Use the MFA folder to complete sign-in.");
console.log("MFA required — mfaToken saved. Use the MFA folder to complete sign-in.");

item.description:
Run order depends on the Login response's `mfaEnrollmentRequired` flag (auto-saved as a collection variable by Login's Test script — check the Postman Console after calling Login to see it logged):

• mfaEnrollmentRequired = true  → 'Enroll TOTP (login) — Start' then '— Confirm'
• mfaEnrollmentRequired = false → 'Verify TOTP (login)', or Send SMS/Email Challenge then Verify SMS/Email OTP, or Verify Backup Code

'TOTP is not enrolled for this account' from Verify TOTP means you skipped enrolment — this account has never confirmed an authenticator. SMS/Email challenges need the backend's SMTP/Twilio configured and reachable; TOTP enroll/verify need no external network call at all, which is the one to use if you're working offline.

request.description: In the 'file' field's Value column, click 'Select Files' and choose any PDF/image to upload — Postman cannot pre-fill a file path. The file is encrypted server-side (AES-256-GCM) before it is written to the active cloud storage provider.
